residency.test: Resident if you have a permanent place of abode and are present at least 30 days in the year, or are present at least 183 days regardless of accommodation.
residency.worldwide_income: There is no personal income tax on employment income, so residence matters mainly for treaty certificates and for business taxation.
residency.note: Residence status does affect whether a non-Saudi carrying on business is subject to the 20% income tax on business profits.

headline.personal_income_tax: none on salary or employment income
headline.business_income: 20% income tax on the non-GCC share of business profits; Zakat of 2.5% on the Saudi and GCC share
headline.gosi: social insurance for Saudi nationals; expatriates are covered only for occupational hazards

income_tax.name: Personal income tax
income_tax.note: Saudi Arabia does not tax individual employment income

employee.name: GOSI (Saudi nationals only)
employee.note: 11.75% for Saudi nationals joining from July 2024 under the reformed scheme, phasing upward; nil for expatriate employees

employer.name: GOSI pension and unemployment (Saudi nationals only)

capital_gains.individuals: no capital gains tax on personal investments for resident individuals
capital_gains.shares: disposals of shares in Saudi listed companies through Tadawul are exempt
capital_gains.business: gains realised by a taxable business form part of the 20% income tax base
capital_gains.non_residents: 20% capital gains tax can apply to non-residents disposing of shares in Saudi companies

quirks: There is no personal income tax, but there is a 15% VAT - among the highest in the region and a real cost of living.

Businesses are taxed under a split system: the share of profit attributable to Saudi and GCC ownership pays Zakat at 2.5%, the non-GCC share pays 20% income tax. Mixed-ownership companies compute both.
Withholding tax of 5% to 20% applies to payments made to non-residents for services, royalties and dividends, and is the most common compliance failure for foreign businesses.
The GOSI reform of July 2024 raised contribution rates for newly joining Saudi nationals on a phased schedule - the rate depends on when the employee first joined.
Real Estate Transaction Tax of 5% applies on property transfers, in place of VAT on real estate.

reporting.who_must_file: Individuals in employment file nothing. Non-Saudi individuals carrying on business in the Kingdom, and entities, must register and file annually.

deadlines.what: Employees have no personal income tax filing obligation
Annual income tax or Zakat return for businesses
VAT returns - monthly above 40m SAR of annual supplies, quarterly below

deadlines.date: First 10 days of the following month
deadlines.what: Withholding tax return on payments to non-residents

forms.name: Annual return for non-GCC owned business income, filed via ZATCA portal
Annual Zakat declaration for Saudi and GCC ownership
Clearance certificate required to renew licences and receive government payments

documents_to_collect: Iqama (residence permit) or national ID and a ZATCA portal account
Commercial registration and licence details if in business
Audited financial statements for the business year
Contracts with non-residents to assess withholding tax
GOSI registration records for all employees
E-invoicing (FATOORA) compliant records - phase two integration is mandatory in waves

penalties.late_filing: 1% of revenue for every 30 days of delay, capped at 20% of the tax due
penalties.late_payment: 1% of the unpaid tax for every 30 days
penalties.vat: 5% to 25% of the tax due, plus fixed penalties for e-invoicing breaches

warnings: This model returns zero personal tax, which is correct for employment income. Business income of non-Saudi individuals is taxable at 20% and is not computed here.
GOSI contributions for Saudi nationals are not modelled.
Expatriate dependent fees and labour levies are employer costs that are not reflected.
